svg.aria-label: How to write ಚ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing ಚ
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಚ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-cha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಚ, 52 frames, 5.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-cha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation writes ಚ in four pen-down runs: from the curled tip inside the head the pen loops up over the head clockwise, slants down to the left, rounds the left lobe and rises into the middle point, drops round the right lobe and climbs the right side, curving over at the top (frames 0–20); after a lift, the lower bar from left to right (frames 24–28); after a second lift, the short link rising from that bar (frame 31); after a third lift, the upper bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 34–39). Its body is ಬ's and its bars are ಕ's. The frames were read from a mirror copy (206×180, 52 frames); no listed size for the Commons file was available to compare it with, so only the slug and the frames were checked. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the head's curled tip is a short wedge, where the path starts, and the right side runs up into the lower bar instead of curving over, so the climb ends at the bar, but the three-lift order remains the same.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 8 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-cha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಚ, 52 frames, 5.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
